label: CCR2004-1G-12S+2XS
description: MikroTik CCR2004-1G-12S+2XS - cloud core router: 1x 1G RJ45, 12x 10G SFP+ cages and 2x 25G SFP28 cages, quad-core ARM AL32400.
notes: MikroTik specification table: section Ethernet prints "10/100/1000 Ethernet ports: 1", section Fiber prints "SFP+ ports: 12" and "Number of 25G SFP28 ports: 2", section Peripherals prints "Serial console port: RJ45". The prose agrees: "12 x 10G SFP+ and 2 x 25G SFP28 ports". The single copper jack is a 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ45 socket and the twelve cages are SFP+, so all three kinds declare their connector. The SFP+ cages are not 10G-only: MikroTik's wired interface compatibility page, section "Devices which SFP+ ports support 1G links", lists "CCR2004-1G-12S+2XS - All SFP+ interfaces can be used in 1G mode if required", so the twelve cages declare speedCaps [1000, 10000] and a 1G SFP uplink terminates on them. The same page, section "Devices which support 2.5G links in SFP/SFP+/SFP28 ports", adds "CCR2004-1G-12S+2XS - All SFP+ and SFP28 interfaces can be used in 2.5G mode if required"; 2.5G is NOT declared here because the cage ladders in engine/media.js carry no 2.5G optical rate (and no 2500BASE-X medium exists in the catalogue), so a 2.5G speedCap would be a number the connector table cannot honour. The two SFP28 cages keep the sfp28 defaults [1000, 10000, 25000]. No PoE in either direction. Sources: https://mikrotik.com/product/ccr2004_1g_12s_2xs , https://manual.mikrotik.com/hardware/ccr2004-1g-12s-plus-2xs/ and https://manual.mikrotik.com/docs/7.25/wired-connections/mikrotik-wired-interface-compatibility/
